title: Revision that actually works
description: Rereading notes feels like revision but mostly is not. Testing yourself, in small doses spread over time, is what makes learning stay.

body.heading: Recall beats rereading
paragraphs: When you reread, everything looks familiar, and familiarity feels like knowledge. The honest test is closing the book and asking: can I actually produce this? That effortful act of recall is what strengthens memory.

Practise with questions, flashcards, or a blank page you fill from memory before checking. Getting things wrong during practice is not failure; it is the mechanism working, because the correction lands harder.

body.heading: Spread it out, keep it small
paragraphs: Several short reviews across days beat one long session the night before, a pattern researchers call the spacing effect. Review a topic a day later, then a few days later, then a week later, widening the gaps as it firms up.
Keep sessions short and mixed: a little of last week's topic alongside today's. It feels harder than rereading, and that feeling of effort is a good sign, not a warning.

takeaway: Close the book, test yourself, and spread short reviews across days.
